title: Proactive throughput contract enforcer with tenant quarantine and staged shedding
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Summary: Implement a proactive throughput contract enforcer for Dedicated pools that guarantees committed throughput while preventing noisy tenants from causing SLO violations for others. The design pairs a deterministic rate-contract allocator (per-tenant/monthly commit translated to tokens/sec), a short-term proactive tenant quarantine that isolates offenders before they overwhelm queues, and a staged shedding policy that demotes traffic gracefully when autoscaler headroom is low.

Goals: (1) Ensure committed throughput guarantees are met 99.9% of the time for committed tenants; (2) Limit cross-tenant latency spikes during bursts; (3) Minimize dropped requests for best-effort tenants while keeping tail latency SLAs intact; (4) Integrate with autoscaler signals so quarantine decisions can be reversed quickly.

Design overview:
- Admission layer enforces deterministic token-bucket contracts per tenant keyed to contract ID. Unconsumed tokens can be soft-borrowed within short windows to absorb spikes.
- When a tenant exceeds an aggressive threshold (sustained borrow > X% for Ys) we place them in a short quarantine window (exponential backoff per offense) that redirects or throttles to best-effort model variants and activates a per-tenant shedder.
- Staged shedding: 1) slow-path (increase queue delay target for tenant), 2) degrade model variant (quantized or small model), 3) hard-drop (when system headroom < critical). Each stage emits structured events to Console and triggers an alert for SRE.
- Autoscaler coupling: quarantine and shedding lower expected instantaneous ingress to allow autoscaler to react. We surface a predicted capacity shortfall metric so autoscaler can prioritize scaling for committed tenants.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict enforcement vs borrowing: strict enforcement protects guarantees but can increase customer-visible errors; allowing borrowing improves customer experience but risks systemic overload. We adopt conservative borrowing (short windows + circuit to quarantine).
- Tenant quarantine vs global shed: quarantining isolates noisy tenants quickly with lower collateral damage than global shed but requires robust tenant identification and rollback behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests showing committed tenant p50/p95 latency within SLO under mixed-burst workload (bench harness linked below).
- Controlled canary across 2 fleets with metrics: committed throughput met >= 99.9%, overall dropped requests <= target for best-effort, and quarantines trigger with correct event logs.
- Integration tests with autoscaler: when deliberate load spike occurs, quarantine reduces peak enough for autoscaler to avoid missing scale-up by more than 1 autoscale step.

Rollout plan: implement feature-gated admission enforcer in ingress, unit tests + perf harness, rollout to internal dedicated pool (canary) for 48h, monitor Grafana dashboard and rollback if committed throughput drops.

Open questions / next steps:
- Finalize borrow window and thresholds after perf runs (current defaults: borrow 10% tokens for 15s, threshold sustained > 60% borrow for 30s -> quarantine).
- Decide whether quarantined traffic should default to model-variant fallback or HTTP 429; proposal: soft-fallback to cheaper model first, escalate to 429 only on repeat offenses.
- Add RBAC for operators to override quarantine for emergency debugging.
